messages.content: Fix the grammar in this, please: Our teacher gave us many homeworks for the holidays.

Our teacher gave us a lot of homework for the holidays.
Why: "Homework" is uncountable, so it has no plural form. Use "a lot of" with it instead of "many", which goes with plural nouns.
My father told that he will come late tonight. Can you check this?

My father said that he will come late tonight.
Why: "Tell" needs a person after it, as in "told me". When no person follows, use "said".
Correct this message to my friend: I didn't went to your party because I was sick.

I didn't go to your party because I was sick.
Why: After "did" or "didn't", use the base form of the verb ("go"), not the past form ("went").
Is anything wrong in this? The soup is very hot, I can't drink it now.

The soup is very hot, so I can't drink it now.
Why: Two complete sentences cannot be joined with only a comma. Add a joining word like "so", or use a full stop.
Please correct: We are going to Goa on next Monday by our car.

We are going to Goa next Monday in our car.
Why: Do not use "on" before "next" or "last" with a day. We say "by car" with nothing in between, but "in our car" when we add "our".
Kindly check my sentence. My boss asked me that why I was late.

My boss asked me why I was late.
Why: In a reported question, the question word ("why") joins the clause by itself. Do not add "that" before it.
I am having a headache since morning, so I will rest. Grammar okay?

I have had a headache since morning, so I will rest.
Why: With "since", for a state that began in the past and is still true now, use the present perfect, not the present continuous.
Could you fix this sentence? I have less coins in my piggy bank than my sister.

I have fewer coins in my piggy bank than my sister.
Why: Use "fewer" with plural nouns you can count, like "coins". Use "less" with uncountable nouns, like "money" or "time".
On Holi, children throws colours on each other and laughs. Please check.

On Holi, children throw colours on each other and laugh.
Why: "Children" is a plural subject, so neither verb takes -s. Both "throw" and "laugh" stay in the base form.
Arjun is the most fastest runner in our school. What should it be?

Arjun is the fastest runner in our school.
Why: "Fastest" is already a superlative because of the -est ending. Do not put "most" in front of it as well.
Look at this sentence: The leaves of this tree turns yellow in winter.

The leaves of this tree turn yellow in winter.
Why: The subject is "leaves", which is plural, so the verb is "turn". The singular word "tree" just before the verb is not the subject.
I have finished reading the book which you gave it to me. Correct?

I have finished reading the book which you gave me.
Why: "Which" already stands for the book. Do not add "it" again inside the same clause.
Can you correct this? I feel very nervous for my exam tomorrow.

I feel very nervous about my exam tomorrow.
Why: We feel nervous "about" something that is coming up. The preposition "for" does not fit here.
It is raining heavily since morning. Is this sentence right?

It has been raining heavily since morning.
Why: The rain started in the past and is still going on. For that, use the present perfect continuous ("has been raining") with "since".
Fix it for me: My room is in the two floor of our house.

My room is on the second floor of our house.
Why: Use the ordinal number "second" when you name a floor. We say "on" a floor, not "in".
Proofread this line: I bought two pair of shoes from the market yesterday.

I bought two pairs of shoes from the market yesterday.
Why: After a number bigger than one, the counting word "pair" must also be plural: "two pairs".
My sister play the guitar and she practise every evening. Please correct it.

My sister plays the guitar and she practises every evening.
Why: "My sister" and "she" are singular subjects. In the present simple, their verbs need -s: "plays" and "practises".
Our dog wag it's tail when we come home. What are the mistakes?

Our dog wags its tail when we come home.
Why: "Its" shows ownership, while "it's" means "it is". A singular subject like "dog" needs "wags" with -s.
My phone's battery died, so I couldn't called you. What's wrong?

My phone's battery died, so I couldn't call you.
Why: After "could" or "couldn't", use the base form of the verb. So "call", not "called".
The principal along with the teachers are coming to the function. Right or wrong?

The principal along with the teachers is coming to the function.
Why: The subject is "the principal", which is singular. A phrase starting with "along with" does not make the subject plural.
Write it correctly: My cousin is elder than me by two years.

My cousin is older than me by two years.
Why: Use "older" when you compare with "than". "Elder" goes before a noun, as in "my elder brother", and is not used with "than".
Neha and Tom was waiting for me at the gate when I reached. Any errors?

Neha and Tom were waiting for me at the gate when I reached.
Why: Two people joined by "and" make a plural subject. A plural subject takes "were", not "was".
Grammar check: Mom, can I have little more of rice please?

Mom, can I have a little more rice please?
Why: "A little" means some, but "little" alone means almost none. Do not put "of" between "more" and a plain noun like "rice".
Our flight got delay and we checked in the hotel after midnight. Can you fix this?

Our flight got delayed and we checked in at the hotel after midnight.
Why: After "got", use the past participle "delayed". We "check in at" a hotel or "check into" it.
How do I fix this? Can you send me the list of participants until tomorrow?

Can you send me the list of participants by tomorrow?
Why: "By" gives a deadline, the latest time something should happen. "Until" means something continues up to that time.
Doctor told me to drink more water and doing some exercise daily. Please correct.

The doctor told me to drink more water and do some exercise daily.
Why: Use "the" before "doctor" when you mean a particular one. After "to", keep both actions in the base form: "drink" and "do".
How much money you spent on the trip? Fix my question.

How much money did you spend on the trip?
Why: A question in the past simple needs "did" before the subject. After "did", the verb goes back to its base form, "spend".
Every year on Eid our neighbour invite us to there home. Is this okay?

Every year on Eid our neighbour invites us to their home.
Why: "Neighbour" is singular, so the verb is "invites". "Their" shows ownership; "there" is about a place.
Who did won the match yesterday? Correct me please.

Who won the match yesterday?
Why: When "who" is the subject of the question, do not use "did". Just use the past form "won".
We saw a peacock dancing in the rain. Its feathers was blue and green. Check the grammar.

We saw a peacock dancing in the rain. Its feathers were blue and green.
Why: "Feathers" is plural, so it takes "were", not "was".
This novel was so interesting that I couldn't stop to read it. Is it correct?

This novel was so interesting that I couldn't stop reading it.
Why: "Stop reading" means you did not end the reading. "Stop to read" means you paused something else in order to read.
Help with this line: I am feeling much happy after talking to you.

I am feeling very happy after talking to you.
Why: "Much" goes with comparatives, as in "much happier". With a plain adjective like "happy", use "very".
Today is very hot weather, so take a umbrella. Please correct both parts.

It is very hot today, so take an umbrella.
Why: "Today" is not weather, so start with "It is". Use "an" before a vowel sound, as in "an umbrella".
Please switch off the fan when you will leave the room. Is this correct English?

Please switch off the fan when you leave the room.
Why: After "when" about the future, use the present simple. Do not put "will" in the "when" part.
Correct the mistake: This shirt is too costly. Can you show me cheaper one?

This shirt is too costly. Can you show me a cheaper one?
Why: "One" here stands for a singular countable noun, "shirt", so it needs the article "a" before "cheaper".
My grandfather listens old songs on the radio every night. Please fix.

My grandfather listens to old songs on the radio every night.
Why: The verb "listen" needs "to" before the thing you hear.
Kavya is having two cats and a parrot. Can you correct this sentence?

Kavya has two cats and a parrot.
Why: "Have" in the sense of owning is a state verb, so it is not used in the -ing form. Use "has".
Please explain me how to save this file. Is the grammar fine?

Please explain to me how to save this file.
Why: "Explain" needs "to" before the person: you explain something to someone.
Ishaan gave a good answer for the teacher's question. What is wrong?

Ishaan gave a good answer to the teacher's question.
Why: We give an answer "to" a question. The preposition "for" does not go with "answer" here.
My uncle and aunt lives in Pune, they have two childs. Please correct this.

My uncle and aunt live in Pune. They have two children.
Why: A subject joined by "and" takes "live" with no -s. The plural of "child" is "children". Two full sentences need a full stop, not a comma.
Sara and I discussed about our plans for the weekend. Is it right?

Sara and I discussed our plans for the weekend.
Why: "Discuss" takes a direct object, so do not add "about" after it. You can say "talked about", but not "discussed about".
This mango is more sweet than the one we ate yesterday. Fix please.

This mango is sweeter than the one we ate yesterday.
Why: Short adjectives form the comparative with -er. So say "sweeter", not "more sweet".
When we reached the station, the train already left. Can you make it correct?

When we reached the station, the train had already left.
Why: The train left first, before we reached. Use the past perfect ("had left") for the earlier of two past actions.
The meeting has been moved to tomorrow because the manager is in leave. Correct?

The meeting has been moved to tomorrow because the manager is on leave.
Why: We say a person is "on leave" when they are away from work. The preposition "in" is wrong here.
After the long walk, my legs were paining a lot. Please correct my English.

After the long walk, my legs were hurting a lot.
Why: In standard English, a body part "hurts" or "aches". "Pain" is mainly used as a noun, as in "I have a pain in my leg".
Can you lend me hundred rupees till Friday? Is this grammatical?

Can you lend me a hundred rupees till Friday?
Why: Do not use "hundred" alone before a noun. Say "a hundred" or "one hundred".
Pongal is a harvest festival which is celebrating in Tamil Nadu. Please check my line.

Pongal is a harvest festival which is celebrated in Tamil Nadu.
Why: The festival does not do the celebrating; people do. So use the passive form "is celebrated".
Both the teams played well, but nobody scored no goals. What is the mistake?

Both the teams played well, but nobody scored any goals.
Why: "Nobody" is already negative. Using "no" as well makes a double negative, so use "any" instead.
I enjoyed to watch the sunset from the hill. Please correct it for me.

I enjoyed watching the sunset from the hill.
Why: "Enjoy" is followed by the -ing form of a verb, not by "to" and a verb.
Who is the writer of this book? I want to read his another book. Fix my second sentence.

Who is the writer of this book? I want to read another of his books.
Why: "Another" cannot come after a possessive like "his". Say "another of his books" or "another book by him".
Rina got angry on me because I forgot her birthday. Please fix the preposition.

Rina got angry with me because I forgot her birthday.
Why: We get angry "with" a person and angry "about" a thing. "Angry on" is not standard English.
Is there any mistake here? The sun rise in the east and set in the west.

The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
Why: Use the present simple for facts that are always true. "The sun" is singular, so both verbs need -s.
I am going to lay down for a while after lunch. Should it be lie?

I am going to lie down for a while after lunch.
Why: "Lie" means to rest your body flat, and it takes no object. "Lay" needs an object: you lay something down.
Which one is cheapest, this bag or that one? Correct my question.

Which one is cheaper, this bag or that one?
Why: When you compare only two things, use the comparative form ("cheaper"). The superlative ("cheapest") is for three or more.
Correct this: My friend has a beautiful voice, she should join to the choir.

My friend has a beautiful voice. She should join the choir.
Why: "Join" takes a direct object, so do not add "to". Two full sentences need a full stop, not a comma.
The puppy is afraid from loud noises. Please edit it.

The puppy is afraid of loud noises.
Why: The adjective "afraid" is followed by "of", not "from". We say "afraid of the dark" or "afraid of dogs".
The website has lots of informations about bus timings. Can you correct it?

The website has lots of information about bus timings.
Why: "Information" is an uncountable noun, so it never takes -s. To count it, say "pieces of information".
Aditi is one of the best student in our class. Is this okay?

Aditi is one of the best students in our class.
Why: "One of the" is always followed by a plural noun, because you pick one from a group.
My sister got married with a doctor last year. What is wrong here?

My sister got married to a doctor last year.
Why: In English, you get married "to" someone, not "with" them. You can also say "She married a doctor".
I am waiting you outside the cinema hall. Fix this message, please.

I am waiting for you outside the cinema hall.
Why: The verb "wait" needs "for" before the person or thing you are waiting for.
Do you know where is the nearest tea stall? Correct this question.

Do you know where the nearest tea stall is?
Why: In a question inside another question, use normal statement order: subject first ("the nearest tea stall"), then the verb ("is").
The luggages were too heavy for the auto. Can you help me correct it?

The luggage was too heavy for the auto.
Why: "Luggage" is uncountable, so it has no plural form. It takes a singular verb: "was", not "were".
I am looking forward to meet you on Monday. Is it correct?

I am looking forward to meeting you on Monday.
Why: In "look forward to", the word "to" is a preposition, not part of a verb. A preposition is followed by the -ing form.
Eating too much sweets are not good for your teeth. Please correct both errors.

Eating too many sweets is not good for your teeth.
Why: "Sweets" is a plural countable noun, so use "many". The subject is the action "eating", which is singular, so use "is".
Anjali spent all her pocket money in books. What should the preposition be?

Anjali spent all her pocket money on books.
Why: We spend money or time "on" something. The preposition "in" does not fit here.
Last Diwali we have bursted many crackers on the terrace. Check this.

Last Diwali we burst many crackers on the terrace.
Why: "Last Diwali" is a finished time, so use the past simple. The past form of "burst" is also "burst"; "bursted" is not standard.
He is good in football but weak at chess. Please correct my sentence.

He is good at football but weak at chess.
Why: We are good "at" a skill or activity. "Good in" is not the usual form for this meaning.
The river was flowing very fastly after the rain. Is this right?

The river was flowing very fast after the rain.
Why: "Fast" is both an adjective and an adverb. The word "fastly" does not exist in standard English.
Can you tell me who has wrote this poem? Is it good English?

Can you tell me who wrote this poem?
Why: "Has wrote" mixes two forms. Use the past simple "wrote", or "has written" with the past participle.
I am sorry for shout at you yesterday. Can you correct this apology?

I am sorry for shouting at you yesterday.
Why: After a preposition like "for", use the -ing form of the verb. So "for shouting", not "for shout".
There was heavy rain in last night and the streets was flooded. What needs fixing?

There was heavy rain last night and the streets were flooded.
Why: Do not use "in" before "last night". "Streets" is plural, so it takes "were".
Who's bag is this on the sofa? I think the spelling is wrong.

Whose bag is this on the sofa?
Why: "Whose" asks who owns something. "Who's" is short for "who is" or "who has", which does not fit here.
The shop was so crowded that we could not hardly move. Fix please.

The shop was so crowded that we could hardly move.
Why: "Hardly" already has a negative meaning. Adding "not" makes a double negative, so drop it.
The concert was began at seven o'clock. How should this be?

The concert began at seven o'clock.
Why: "Was began" mixes the passive and the past simple. Here the concert simply started, so use the past simple "began".
My cat sleeps on my bed every nights. Is there a mistake?

My cat sleeps on my bed every night.
Why: "Every" is always followed by a singular noun. So "every night", not "every nights".
Can you teach me how to use this camera? I am new in photography. Please correct.

Can you teach me how to use this camera? I am new to photography.
Why: When you have just started an activity, you are new "to" it. "New in" is used for places, as in "new in town".
If I studied harder, I would have passed the test. Something feels off, right?

If I had studied harder, I would have passed the test.
Why: This is about an unreal past. With "would have passed" in the result, the "if" part needs the past perfect: "had studied".
My mother make the best parathas in whole family. Can you check it?

My mother makes the best parathas in the whole family.
Why: "My mother" is singular, so the verb takes -s. We say "the whole family", with "the".
Zoya suggested to watch a movie on Sunday. Correct my sentence.

Zoya suggested watching a movie on Sunday.
Why: "Suggest" is followed by the -ing form, not "to" and a verb. You can also say "Zoya suggested that we watch a movie".
The vegetables in the market is very fresh today. Any errors?

The vegetables in the market are very fresh today.
Why: The subject is "vegetables", which is plural, so use "are". "Market" is not the subject.
How long it takes to reach Mysore from Bangalore by bus? Please correct the question.

How long does it take to reach Mysore from Bangalore by bus?
Why: A present simple question needs "does" before the subject "it". After "does", use the base form "take".
Mr Fernandes is senior than me in the office. Is that correct?

Mr Fernandes is senior to me in the office.
Why: "Senior" and "junior" are followed by "to", not "than". They are not -er comparatives.
My grandmother can't able to walk long distances now. Please fix this.

My grandmother can't walk long distances now.
Why: "Can" and "able to" mean the same thing, so use only one. You could also say "isn't able to walk".
He gave me a five hundred rupees note. Should "rupees" be singular?

He gave me a five-hundred-rupee note.
Why: When a number and a noun describe another noun, the noun stays singular and the words are joined with hyphens.
Although it was raining, but people still came to the Ganesh festival. What is the error?

Although it was raining, people still came to the Ganesh festival.
Why: "Although" and "but" both show a contrast. Use only one of them in a sentence, not both.
Lena runs faster then her brother. Check my spelling, please.

Lena runs faster than her brother.
Why: Use "than" when you compare two things. "Then" is about time or order, as in "first this, then that".
Monkeys was jumping from one tree to other. Please correct the grammar.

Monkeys were jumping from one tree to another.
Why: "Monkeys" is plural, so it takes "were". The usual pattern is "from one ... to another".
The author describes the village very beautiful. Is the grammar right?

The author describes the village very beautifully.
Why: The word tells us how the author describes, so it must be an adverb. Add -ly: "beautifully".
I am very much worry about my brother's exam. Help me fix it.

I am very worried about my brother's exam.
Why: After "am", you need the adjective "worried". "Worry" is a verb or a noun, not an adjective.
In winter the days becomes short and the nights long. Correct me, please.

In winter the days become short and the nights long.
Why: "Days" is a plural subject, so the verb has no -s: "become", not "becomes".
Somebody have left the gate open again. Is this sentence right?

Somebody has left the gate open again.
Why: "Somebody" is singular, even though it can mean any person. A singular subject takes "has", not "have".
I returned back the dress because it didn't fit. Please improve the grammar.

I returned the dress because it didn't fit.
Why: "Return" already means to give or take something back. Adding "back" repeats the same idea.
Everyone in our family love old Hindi songs. Can you correct it?

Everyone in our family loves old Hindi songs.
Why: "Everyone" is singular in grammar, even though it means many people. So the verb takes -s: "loves".
Our parrot can speak few words, like hello and mango. What should I change?

Our parrot can speak a few words, like hello and mango.
Why: "A few" means some. "Few" alone means almost none, which is not what you mean here.
My brother is very good with computers, he can repairs any laptop. Please fix.

My brother is very good with computers. He can repair any laptop.
Why: After "can", use the base form "repair". Two full sentences need a full stop, not a comma.
The teacher made us to write the essay again. Is "to" needed?

The teacher made us write the essay again.
Why: After "make" and a person, use the base verb without "to". So "made us write", not "made us to write".
My little brother always insists to sit by the window. Correct this line.

My little brother always insists on sitting by the window.
Why: "Insist" is followed by "on" and the -ing form. It does not take "to" and a verb.
Did you hear the news? Jake have got a new job. Check my grammar.

Did you hear the news? Jake has got a new job.
Why: "Jake" is one person, so use "has", not "have". "Have" goes with I, you, we and they.
Can I get an glass of water and a idli? Fix the articles.

Can I get a glass of water and an idli?
Why: Use "a" before a consonant sound, as in "a glass". Use "an" before a vowel sound, as in "an idli".
We stayed in a hotel which owner was very friendly. What is wrong?

We stayed in a hotel whose owner was very friendly.
Why: To show that something belongs to the noun before it, use "whose". "Which" cannot show ownership.
My colleague is used to wake up at five every day. Can you correct it?

My colleague is used to waking up at five every day.
Why: "Be used to" means "be in the habit of". In this phrase, "to" is a preposition, so the -ing form follows.
My father has gave up tea and now he drinks only water at night. Please check.

My father has given up tea and now he drinks only water at night.
Why: The present perfect is "has" plus the past participle. The past participle of "give" is "given", not "gave".
Between you and I, I spent too much at the fair. Is this grammatical?

Between you and me, I spent too much at the fair.
Why: "Between" is a preposition, so it is followed by object pronouns. Use "me", not "I".
Each and every students took part in the Republic Day parade. Fix it, please.

Each and every student took part in the Republic Day parade.
Why: "Each" and "every" are followed by a singular noun. So "every student", not "every students".
Our coach said we must to practise even on Sundays. What is the mistake?

Our coach said we must practise even on Sundays.
Why: "Must" is a modal verb. Like "can" and "should", it is followed by the base verb without "to".
The nature is very beautiful in the hills. Do I need "the"?

Nature is very beautiful in the hills.
Why: When "nature" means the natural world in general, it does not take "the".
This book is consisted of twelve short stories. Please correct the verb.

This book consists of twelve short stories.
Why: "Consist of" is never used in the passive. Say "consists of" or "is made up of".
We have done a mistake in the last sum. Is that the right verb?

We have made a mistake in the last sum.
Why: In English, we "make" a mistake, not "do" one. Some words always go with "make", and "mistake" is one of them.
My grandfather was born at 1950 in a small village. Correct the preposition.

My grandfather was born in 1950 in a small village.
Why: Use "in" with years, months and seasons. Use "at" with clock times, as in "at six o'clock".
Peter and Ananya enjoyed themself at the fair. Is the last word right?

Peter and Ananya enjoyed themselves at the fair.
Why: The subject is two people, so the reflexive pronoun must be plural: "themselves".
I like very much spicy food. How do I say this correctly?

I like spicy food very much.
Why: In English, "very much" does not go between the verb and its object. Put it after the object.
Please bring this parcel to the post office when you go out. Is "bring" right?

Please take this parcel to the post office when you go out.
Why: Use "take" for moving something away from where you are now. Use "bring" for moving it towards you.
All the staffs were present at the meeting. Please correct it.

All the staff were present at the meeting.
Why: "Staff" already means a group of workers, so it does not take -s. To count them, say "staff members".
I wish I can sleep earlier, but my neighbours are noisy. What is wrong?

I wish I could sleep earlier, but my neighbours are noisy.
Why: After "I wish" about a present situation you want to change, use a past form. So "could", not "can".
The price of onions have gone up again. Is the verb correct?

The price of onions has gone up again.
Why: The subject is "the price", which is singular, so use "has". "Onions" is not the subject.
Navratri is lasting nine nights every year. Can you fix the tense?

Navratri lasts nine nights every year.
Why: "Every year" shows a regular fact, so use the present simple. The present continuous is for things happening right now.
Who is better player, Maya or Ruth? Check my question.

Who is the better player, Maya or Ruth?
Why: When you compare two named people or things, use "the" before the comparative: "the better player".
Look! The birds flies south. Please correct this.

Look! The birds are flying south.
Why: "Look!" shows that it is happening now, so use the present continuous. "Birds" is plural, so use "are".
Mrs Rao teached us this poem in class six. Find the error.

Mrs Rao taught us this poem in class six.
Why: "Teach" is an irregular verb. Its past form is "taught", not "teached".
I felt proud when my friends congratulated me for winning the debate. Is it correct?

I felt proud when my friends congratulated me on winning the debate.
Why: We congratulate someone "on" something they did, not "for" it.
Despite of the fog, the buses ran on time. What should I change?

Despite the fog, the buses ran on time.
Why: "Despite" is not followed by "of". You can say "despite the fog" or "in spite of the fog".
My mother asked me to do the bed before school. Is "do" correct here?

My mother asked me to make the bed before school.
Why: In English, we "make the bed". It is a fixed phrase, so "do" sounds wrong.
I want to buy a red big umbrella for the rains. Is the word order okay?

I want to buy a big red umbrella for the rains.
Why: When you use more than one adjective, size usually comes before colour. So "big red", not "red big".
I could of joined the band if I had practised more. Is "could of" right?

I could have joined the band if I had practised more.
Why: "Could of" is a spelling mistake. It comes from the short form "could've", which means "could have".
Don't loose the dog's leash again. Check the spelling.

Don't lose the dog's leash again.
Why: "Lose" means to stop having something or to be unable to find it. "Loose" means not tight.
The printer stopped working, may be there is no ink. Please correct.

The printer stopped working. Maybe there is no ink.
Why: "Maybe", as one word, means "perhaps". "May be" is a verb form. Two full sentences need a full stop, not a comma.
Our school has an university next to it. Is "an" right?

Our school has a university next to it.
Why: "University" begins with a "yoo" sound, which is a consonant sound. So use "a", not "an".
Does your mother likes gardening? Fix the verb please.

Does your mother like gardening?
Why: In a question with "does", the -s is already on "does". The main verb stays in the base form: "like".
Myself Ritika, and I am new in this class. Is this a good introduction?

I am Ritika, and I am new in this class.
Why: "Myself" is a reflexive pronoun. It cannot be the subject, so introduce yourself with "I am" or "My name is".
Two dozens eggs were broken in the box. Any mistake?

Two dozen eggs were broken in the box.
Why: After a number, "dozen" stays singular, just like "hundred". So "two dozen eggs".
She has went to Kolkata for a wedding. Correct this.

She has gone to Kolkata for a wedding.
Why: "Has" needs the past participle of the verb. The past participle of "go" is "gone", not "went".
I am agree with your plan for the project. Please fix my grammar.

I agree with your plan for the project.
Why: "Agree" is a verb, so it does not need "am" before it. Say "I agree", not "I am agree".
My sister hurt her hand, so she went to doctor. What is missing?

My sister hurt her hand, so she went to the doctor.
Why: We say "go to the doctor", with "the". "Doctor" is a countable noun and needs an article.
Many people prefers saving money than spending it. Please correct both errors.

Many people prefer saving money to spending it.
Why: "People" is plural, so the verb has no -s. We "prefer" one thing "to" another, not "than".
We went to see the Durga Puja pandals and come back very late. Is the tense right?

We went to see the Durga Puja pandals and came back very late.
Why: The whole story is in the past, so both verbs should be in the past simple: "went" and "came".
Ali plays the cricket every evening with his friends. Check it.

Ali plays cricket every evening with his friends.
Why: Do not use "the" before the name of a sport. Say "play cricket" or "play football".
The garden is full of flowers which smells lovely. Correct please.

The garden is full of flowers which smell lovely.
Why: "Which" refers to "flowers", which is plural. So the verb takes no -s: "smell".
Can you suggest me a good book for a long train journey? Is it okay?

Can you suggest a good book for a long train journey?
Why: "Suggest" does not take a person right after it. If you want to add the person, say "suggest a good book to me".
I was very tired, but I felt so happy that I can't stop smiling. What is wrong?

I was very tired, but I felt so happy that I couldn't stop smiling.
Why: The sentence is about the past, so keep every verb in the past. Use "couldn't", not "can't".
The weather was so nice that we decided to go for picnic. Please fix.

The weather was so nice that we decided to go for a picnic.
Why: "Picnic" is a singular countable noun, so it needs an article. Say "go for a picnic".
There is much people in our building who keep pets. Correct my sentence.

There are many people in our building who keep pets.
Why: "People" is a plural countable noun. So use "are" and "many", not "is" and "much".
I lost my wallet at the mall and I am searching it everywhere. Check this.

I lost my wallet at the mall and I am searching for it everywhere.
Why: You "search" a place, but you "search for" the thing you have lost. The wallet is the lost thing.
I and my cousin performed a song at the wedding. Is the order right?

My cousin and I performed a song at the wedding.
Why: In English, it is polite to name the other person first and put "I" last.
The rabbit hided under the bed when the guests came. Fix the verb.

The rabbit hid under the bed when the guests came.
Why: "Hide" is an irregular verb. Its past form is "hid", not "hided".
My laptop is too much slow these days. How do I say this?

My laptop is very slow these days.
Why: "Too much" goes before a noun, as in "too much noise". Before an adjective like "slow", use "very" or "too" alone.
Mathematics are my favourite subject. Is this right?

Mathematics is my favourite subject.
Why: Names of subjects that end in -s, like "mathematics" and "physics", are singular. So they take "is".
My cousin is ten years old boy who loves puzzles. Correct the sentence.

My cousin is a ten-year-old boy who loves puzzles.
Why: Before a noun, the age phrase is joined with hyphens and "year" stays singular. "Boy" also needs the article "a".
Tara asked me where was I going. Is the word order right?

Tara asked me where I was going.
Why: In reported questions, use statement order: subject first ("I"), then the verb ("was").
This dal tastes deliciously. Correct it for me.

This dal tastes delicious.
Why: Here "taste" works like "be": it links the subject to a describing word. So use the adjective "delicious", not the adverb.
We were boarding the bus when suddenly it start raining. Please correct.

We were boarding the bus when suddenly it started raining.
Why: The sudden action happened in the past, so use the past simple "started".
Teacher marked this wrong in my diary: I was too happy to see my old friend at the station. Why?

I was very happy to see my old friend at the station.
Why: "Too" means more than is good or possible. "Too happy to see" would mean you were so happy that you could not see. Use "very".
Sometime it snows in Shimla in December, but not every year. Is the first word right?

Sometimes it snows in Shimla in December, but not every year.
Why: "Sometimes" means now and then. "Sometime" means at a time that is not known, as in "Let's meet sometime".
When I entered into the kitchen, the milk had boiled over. Please correct.

When I entered the kitchen, the milk had boiled over.
Why: "Enter" takes a direct object, so do not add "into" after it. Say "entered the room" or "went into the room".
The shopkeeper told us a good news: the sale starts tomorrow. Fix my English.

The shopkeeper told us some good news: the sale starts tomorrow.
Why: "News" is uncountable, even though it ends in -s. Do not use "a" with it; use "some" or "a piece of".
I seen her play the sitar at the school function. What should it be?

I saw her play the sitar at the school function.
Why: "Seen" is the past participle, and it needs "have" or "has" before it. For a simple past action, use "saw".
My uncle keeps three sheeps and a goat as pets. Is the plural right?

My uncle keeps three sheep and a goat as pets.
Why: "Sheep" has the same form in the singular and the plural. So "one sheep" and "three sheep".
Would you mind to send me the link again? Please correct the request.

Would you mind sending me the link again?
Why: "Mind" is followed by the -ing form of a verb, not by "to" and a verb.
Please answer to all the questions in full sentences. Is "to" needed here?

Please answer all the questions in full sentences.
Why: The verb "answer" takes a direct object, so drop "to". Only the noun takes "to", as in "the answer to the question".
My little sister resembles to our grandmother. Correct this line.

My little sister resembles our grandmother.
Why: "Resemble" takes a direct object. Do not put "to" after it.
Lucas, please reply me when you see this message. Can you fix it?

Lucas, please reply to me when you see this message.
Why: "Reply" needs "to" before the person or thing you are answering. So "reply to me".
The knifes in this kitchen are not sharp enough to cut tomatoes. Spelling check, please.

The knives in this kitchen are not sharp enough to cut tomatoes.
Why: Many nouns ending in -fe or -f change to -ves in the plural. So "knife" becomes "knives".
Unless it doesn't rain, we will go trekking tomorrow. Does this make sense?

Unless it rains, we will go trekking tomorrow.
Why: "Unless" already means "if not". Adding "doesn't" makes a double negative and reverses the meaning you want.
I joined this company before three years. What is the correct way?

I joined this company three years ago.
Why: Use "ago" to count back from now. Use "before" with another time or event, as in "before the meeting".
My grandmother avoids to eat fried food at night. Please fix the verb.

My grandmother avoids eating fried food at night.
Why: "Avoid" is followed by the -ing form of a verb. It does not take "to" and a verb.
My savings is more than my brother's because I don't buy snacks. Correct me.

My savings are more than my brother's because I don't buy snacks.
Why: "Savings" in this sense is a plural noun, so it takes "are", not "is".
We lit diyas and drawed a rangoli outside the door. Which word is wrong?

We lit diyas and drew a rangoli outside the door.
Why: "Draw" is an irregular verb. Its past form is "drew", not "drawed".
Simran has a lot of sports equipments in her room. Please correct.

Simran has a lot of sports equipment in her room.
Why: "Equipment" is uncountable, so it never takes -s. To count it, say "pieces of equipment".
The sky was quiet clear, so we could see many stars. Spot the error.

The sky was quite clear, so we could see many stars.
Why: "Quite" means fairly or very. "Quiet" means making little or no noise. The two words are easy to mix up.
Most of books in our library are in Hindi or English. Is it grammatical?

Most of the books in our library are in Hindi or English.
Why: After "most of", use "the" or a word like "my" before the noun. Without "of", you can just say "most books".
Arun doesn't like when people interrupt him. Is anything missing?

Arun doesn't like it when people interrupt him.
Why: "Like" needs an object. Add "it" to stand for the situation that the "when" part describes.
I don't know weather it will rain tomorrow. Please correct the spelling.

I don't know whether it will rain tomorrow.
Why: "Whether" means "if" and introduces a choice. "Weather" is the noun for rain, sun and wind.
Let's to clean the balcony this Sunday. What is wrong?

Let's clean the balcony this Sunday.
Why: "Let's" is followed by the base form of the verb, without "to".
You're bag is still on the counter, ma'am. Did I write it right?

Your bag is still on the counter, ma'am.
Why: "Your" shows that something belongs to you. "You're" is short for "you are", which does not fit here.
The singer raised from her chair and bowed to the audience. Correct it, please.

The singer rose from her chair and bowed to the audience.
Why: "Rise" means to go up by yourself and takes no object. "Raise" means to lift something else, so it needs an object.
Our dog barks whenever he hear the doorbell. Please check.

Our dog barks whenever he hears the doorbell.
Why: "He" is a singular subject, so the present simple verb needs -s: "hears".
The phone I buyed last month has stopped charging. Find the mistake.

The phone I bought last month has stopped charging.
Why: "Buy" is an irregular verb. Its past form is "bought", not "buyed".
Our teacher told us to don't run in the corridor. Is the negative right?

Our teacher told us not to run in the corridor.
Why: To make "to" plus a verb negative, put "not" before "to". So "not to run", not "to don't run".
My both brothers study in Delhi. Please fix the order.

Both my brothers study in Delhi.
Why: "Both" comes before words like "my", "the" and "these". So say "both my brothers", not "my both brothers".
Let me introduce you my friend Kiara. Is this correct?

Let me introduce you to my friend Kiara.
Why: You introduce one person "to" another person. So the word "to" is needed before "my friend".
Please give me a bread and some butter. Correct the article.

Please give me some bread and some butter.
Why: "Bread" is uncountable, so do not use "a" with it. Say "some bread" or "a slice of bread".
Our hotel room had a beautiful scenery of the lake. Grammar check, please.

Our hotel room had a beautiful view of the lake.
Why: "Scenery" is uncountable and does not take "a". For what you see from one place, use "view".
Please make sure all of you attends the training on Friday. Is the verb right?

Please make sure all of you attend the training on Friday.
Why: "All of you" is a plural subject, so the verb takes no -s: "attend".
Rehan hurt his foot, so he is not able to walk proper. How should it end?

Rehan hurt his foot, so he is not able to walk properly.
Why: The word describes how he walks, so it must be an adverb. Use "properly", not "proper".
Ritu was robbed her purse on the bus. Is this sentence correct?

Ritu's purse was stolen on the bus.
Why: You "steal" a thing, but you "rob" a person or a place. Since the purse is the thing taken, use "stolen".
Christmas is celebrated on 25 December in all over the world. What should I remove?

Christmas is celebrated on 25 December all over the world.
Why: "All over the world" already tells us where. Do not put "in" before it.
Neither Kunal nor Arjun know the rules of chess. Is the verb correct?

Neither Kunal nor Arjun knows the rules of chess.
Why: With "neither ... nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Arjun" is singular, so use "knows".
Hundreds of birds migrates to this lake every winter. Correct my sentence.

Hundreds of birds migrate to this lake every winter.
Why: The subject is "hundreds of birds", which is plural. So the verb takes no -s: "migrate".
The story is about a girl who lose her way in a forest. Please fix it.

The story is about a girl who loses her way in a forest.
Why: "Who" refers to "a girl", which is singular. So the verb needs -s: "loses".
Ruth feels nervous whenever she has to speak infront of the class. Spelling?

Ruth feels nervous whenever she has to speak in front of the class.
Why: "In front of" is written as three separate words. "Infront" is not a word.
Look at the dark clouds! It is going to raining soon. Please correct the second sentence.

Look at the dark clouds! It is going to rain soon.
Why: "Going to" for the future is followed by the base form of the verb. So "going to rain", not "going to raining".
I put the keys on the table, but now I can't find it. What is wrong?

I put the keys on the table, but now I can't find them.
Why: A pronoun must match the noun it stands for. "Keys" is plural, so use "them", not "it".
This trousers are too long for me. Can you fix the first word?

These trousers are too long for me.
Why: "Trousers" is a plural noun, like "jeans" and "scissors". So use "these", not "this".
My brother hears music while he studies. Is "hears" the right verb?

My brother listens to music while he studies.
Why: "Hear" means sounds reach your ears. "Listen to" means you pay attention on purpose, which fits here.
The cat is sitting besides the window all morning. Correct both mistakes.

The cat has been sitting beside the window all morning.
Why: "Beside" means next to; "besides" means "also". For an action that started earlier and is still going on, use "has been sitting".
I need to charge my phone, the battery is almost die. Please correct this.

I need to charge my phone. The battery is almost dead.
Why: After "is", you need the adjective "dead", not the verb "die". Two full sentences need a full stop, not a comma.
Our class teacher is very strict, but she is also very kind with us. Is the preposition okay?

Our class teacher is very strict, but she is also very kind to us.
Why: We are kind "to" a person. The preposition "with" does not go with "kind" in this meaning.
My mother has three sisters, and all of them is teachers. Check this.

My mother has three sisters, and all of them are teachers.
Why: "All of them" refers to the three sisters, so it is plural. Use "are", not "is".
Siddharth asked me to help him for his project. Is "for" right?

Siddharth asked me to help him with his project.
Why: You help someone "with" a task or a problem. "For" does not fit after "help him" here.
I don't like neither tea nor coffee. Help me fix it.

I like neither tea nor coffee.
Why: "Neither ... nor" is already negative, so do not add "don't". You can also say "I don't like tea or coffee".
Where you will stay in London next month? Correct the question, please.

Where will you stay in London next month?
Why: In a question with a word like "where", put the helping verb "will" before the subject "you".
